diagram_math_checks.details: The Example specializes the existing F1 supplier to d=2 and one scalar constraint: q,p in R^2, c:R^2 -> R with c(q)=(q^Tq-ell^2)/2, J(q):R^2 -> R equal to q^T, and scalar lambda. Thus the drawn configuration locus is the complete circle ||q||=ell, and tangent momentum obeys q^Tp=0 since M=mI_2. No new map or commutative-square assertion is introduced.

In diagram coordinates the bob is (0.78,-1.04), whose squared norm is 1.69=1.3^2, on the circle centered at the pivot. The p arrow displacement is (0.728,0.546); its dot product with the radius is 0.78*0.728-1.04*0.546=0. Hence it is genuinely tangent. The vector q points from the origin to the bob, while p starts at the bob. Drawing coordinates merely set the position scale ell/1.3.
diagram_math_checks.local_justification: Example constraint and consistency hypothesis; Verification step 1.1

diagram_math_checks.details: The bob is the bottom point (0,-ell) and p=0. F1 gives dot p=-grad V-J^T lambda=-mg e_2-lambda q. With lambda=mg/ell from step 2.1, -lambda q=+mg e_2, so force arrows point upward and downward with equal lengths (0.9 drawing units each), and their sum is zero. The caption explicitly restricts the illustrated arrow directions to g>0, without changing the original Example. Position and force scales are explicitly distinguished.

Both loci use native circle paths and are visibly closed; all shown pivot/bob state markers are solid points, not excluded endpoints. The right panel has zero momentum and no momentum arrow. There is no trajectory, graph-edge relation, crossing, time evolution or generic tension-sign assertion. The original two-step verification remains an exact byte-preserved prefix and proves the assertions independently.
